title: Bravo !
subtitle: Four ways to say well done
review: Written by Claude. Check the French, the English lines, the notes and the questions.
intro: A light bulb changed after three months, a driving test passed at the fifth attempt, a pancake that does not come back down and a new job that has to be celebrated: four short scenes between Emma and Lucas. Listen for how they congratulate each other, and for the moments when the praise is not entirely sincere.

lines.text: Ça y est ! J'ai changé l'ampoule !

tr.en: Done it! I've changed the light bulb!

lines.note: Ça y est: it's done, at last.

tr.en: Well done!

lines.note: Bravo: for something a person has done.

tr.en: All by myself. Without the instructions.

lines.note: La notice: the instruction leaflet.

tr.en: Nicely done! Hats off!

lines.note: Chapeau: 'hats off'. Said with respect or, as here, with a smile.

tr.en: Are you making fun of me?

lines.note: Se moquer de: to make fun of.

lines.text: Pas du tout. Toutes mes félicitations !

tr.en: Not at all. My warmest congratulations!

lines.note: Toutes mes félicitations is formal, which is the joke: it was only a light bulb.

tr.en: Thank you. It wasn't easy.

lines.note: Spoken French drops ne: ce n'était pas facile.

lines.text: Je sais. Ça fait trois mois que j'attends.

tr.en: I know. I've been waiting for three months.

lines.note: Ça fait + time + que + present: for an action that is still going on.

tr.en: Lucas! I've passed my driving test!

lines.note: Le permis: the driving licence. Avoir son permis: to pass the test.

lines.text: Non ! Bravo ! Tu l'as bien mérité.

tr.en: No! Well done! You really earned it.

lines.note: Mériter: to deserve. Tu l'as bien mérité credits the work, not only the result.

tr.en: At the fifth attempt…

lines.text: Justement. Tous tes efforts ont payé.

tr.en: Exactly. All your hard work paid off.

lines.note: Justement turns her point round: five attempts prove the effort.

tr.en: That's true.

lines.text: Je savais que tu y arriverais. Tu peux être fière de toi.

tr.en: I knew you'd do it. You can be proud of yourself.

lines.note: Y arriver: to manage it. Fière takes -e: he is talking to a woman.

lines.text: Merci. Tu me prêtes ta voiture ?

tr.en: Thanks. Will you lend me your car?

lines.note: Prêter: to lend.

tr.en: … Congratulations. But no.

lines.text: Regarde ! Je fais sauter la crêpe.

tr.en: Watch! I'm tossing the pancake.

lines.note: Faire sauter: to make it jump, to toss.

tr.en: Go on!
And up!

lines.note: Hop: the sound of a quick movement.

tr.en: Wow! You nailed it!

lines.note: T'as = tu as. Assurer: to do it really well. Slang.

tr.en: Wait, the second one. Up!
Amazing! You handled that!

lines.note: Trop fort: 'so good'. Gérer: to manage something well. Slang.

lines.text: Et la troisième… Hop ! … Elle est où ?

tr.en: And the third one… Up! … Where is it?
On the ceiling. You smashed it.

lines.note: T'as déchiré: 'you smashed it'. Emma says it without a smile: irony.

lines.text: J'ai une grande nouvelle. J'ai le poste !

tr.en: I've got big news. I got the job!

lines.note: Le poste: the job, the position.

tr.en: No! What great news!

lines.note: Quelle + noun: what a…!

tr.en: I start on Monday.

lines.text: Félicitations pour ton nouveau poste ! Je suis trop content pour toi !

tr.en: Congratulations on your new job! I'm so happy for you!

lines.note: Félicitations pour + noun. Trop here means 'so', not 'too'.

tr.en: Thank you, darling.

lines.text: Je suis fier de toi. Ça se fête ! Restaurant ?

tr.en: I'm proud of you. This calls for a celebration! Restaurant?

lines.note: Ça se fête: that should be celebrated. Fier without -e: a man is speaking.

tr.en: Good idea! Is it your treat?

lines.note: Inviter quelqu'un: to pay for that person.

lines.text: Ah non. C'est toi qui as le nouveau salaire.

tr.en: Oh no. You're the one with the new salary.

lines.note: C'est toi qui as: the verb agrees with toi.

notes: Bravo and bien joué praise something a person did. Félicitations is for a success or a life event: an exam, a job, a wedding.
Chapeau and toutes mes félicitations are strong. Used for a small thing, they tease.
Tu l'as bien mérité and tous tes efforts ont payé praise the work behind the result.
T'as assuré, t'as géré, t'as déchiré and trop fort are slang, for friends. T'as = tu as.
Fier, content for a man; fière, contente for a woman: je suis fier de toi, tu peux être fière de toi.
Ça se fête ! proposes a celebration. If you say je t'invite, you are paying.

questions.q: Your colleague has a new job. What do you write on the card?
questions.why: Félicitations pour + the event. The slang stays off the office card.

questions.q: Emma passed at the fifth attempt. Lucas wants to praise her effort. What does he say?
questions.why: Tous tes efforts ont payé: all your hard work paid off.

questions.q: Lucas says « Tu peux être fière de toi ». Why fière and not fier?
questions.why: The adjective agrees with the person: fier for a man, fière for a woman.

questions.q: The pancake is on the ceiling and Emma says « T'as déchiré ». What does she mean?
options: She is angry about the job.
questions.why: T'as déchiré means 'you smashed it'. Said flatly about a failure, it is irony.

questions.q: « Ça se fête ! » What is Lucas suggesting?
questions.why: Ça se fête: that calls for a celebration.
